lessons.title: Arithmetic Progression (AP)
lessons.concept: An arithmetic progression is a sequence where the difference between consecutive terms is constant. This constant is called the common difference (d).
lessons.formula: nth term: a_n = a + (n-1)d. Sum of first n terms: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n-1)d] = n/2 (a + l), where a is first term and l is last term.
mistakes: Using n instead of (n-1) in the nth term formula
Sign errors when common difference is negative
Confusing term value with term index

lessons.title: Geometric Progression (GP)
lessons.concept: A geometric progression is a sequence where each term after the first is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a constant called the common ratio (r).
lessons.formula: nth term: a_n = a*r^(n-1). Sum of first n terms (r != 1): S_n = a*(r^n - 1)/(r - 1).
mistakes: Confusing common ratio with common difference
Applying GP sum formula incorrectly when r=1
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Identifying AP and GP
lessons.concept: To identify the type of progression, check differences and ratios between consecutive terms. Constant difference indicates AP; constant ratio indicates GP. Some sequences may be neither.
lessons.formula: AP check: a2-a1 = a3-a2 = ... = d. GP check: a2/a1 = a3/a2 = ... = r (terms non-zero).
lessons.worked_example: Sequence 4, 7, 10, 13 has constant difference +3, so AP. Sequence 2, 6, 18, 54 has constant ratio 3, so GP.
mistakes: Checking only one pair of terms and assuming the pattern holds
Labeling a non-constant sequence as AP/GP
